title: Casa Noy
subtitle: Wood and stone villa at the jungle's edge
description:
Here, the jungle of the Riviera Maya stops at the edge of the terrace. Behind a limestone wall and broad tropical leaves, Casa Noy raises a mineral facade, cut by tall wooden doors with a deep grain. From the entrance, the house says a great deal with very little: concrete, stone, wood, and the green of the canopy behind every glass wall.

Inside, the materials stay honest and invite the hand. Board formed concrete keeps the imprint of its planks on the walls, and a floating staircase rises above steps that carry heavy blocks of solid wood. Tropical wood returns throughout, on the floor to ceiling doors as in the kitchen, where it meets a veined stone backsplash and anthracite cabinetry. The bedrooms look out onto greenery. There are six, five with ensuite bathrooms, and the sixth adapts to its owner: home office, art studio or guest room.

Outside, a pergola of wooden slats filters the sun over the terrace and the outdoor living area. The private pool, lined in natural stone, takes on the color of cenote water. Palms, elephant ears and the tall trees of the jungle keep the house in shade and away from view. Above, the rooftop terrace opens to the Caribbean sky and the green of the treetops. Multiple parking spaces and two storage rooms complete the property, for full time living as well as extended stays.

Puerto Aventuras, a gated community of the Riviera Maya, lives to the rhythm of its marina, its nine hole golf course, its restaurants and its beach clubs. All around, nature remains the great wealth of the region: the Maya jungle, cenotes with crystal clear water, and the Caribbean Sea, along the second largest coral reef in the world. Playa del Carmen, Tulum and Cancún International Airport are all within easy reach by road. A home for family life or a lasting investment in the Mexican Caribbean.
